source.title: Benign Overfitting in Deep Neural Networks under Lazy Training
source.authors: Zhen-Yu Zhu; Fanghui Liu; Grigorios G. Chrysos; Francesco Locatello; V. Cevher

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figure text are garbled, but the classification results and Theorem 4 are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives a theoretical result for SGD training of randomly initialized deep ReLU networks on noisy binary classification data. It studies training loss rather than benchmark training classification error and does not run the benchmark experiments in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper also states that MNIST experiments verify an NTK assumption; those measure kernel values, not training error. Statements about prior work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study proves convergence for fully connected ReLU networks on bounded, separated binary-classification data. V1 specifies convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100; the study provides no results for those systems or datasets. It does not test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' classification conclusion: under their assumptions and lazy training, deep ReLU networks can fit noisy training labels while approaching Bayes-optimal test error. Their regression conclusion additionally concerns excess-risk bounds depending on label noise and initialization noise.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD from Gaussian initialization with logistic loss on fully connected ReLU networks under a lazy-training analysis; this is not a benchmark reproduction and does not test CIFAR or Adam.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee depends on the stated data assumptions, network width, step size, maximum iterations, and lazy-training regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4 guarantees empirical logistic loss at most δ with high probability for sufficiently wide, randomly initialized fully connected ReLU networks trained by SGD, assuming bounded inputs and separation of oppositely labeled examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide fully connected ReLU networks can reach arbitrarily small training logistic loss under bounded-input and label-separation assumptions with suitable SGD step sizes and iteration budgets.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202, 2023
record.problems: The classification result is theoretical and depends on stated distribution and network assumptions. No benchmark training-error experiment or empirical comparison is reported for this claim. The theorem states only “with high probability” without a numeric probability.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows omitted. The MNIST kernel-value figure checks an NTK assumption, not a training outcome; cited results are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels and the stated model-size and training-recipe comparisons.
Spurious local minima and the effect of adding student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or the stated alternative training recipes.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Effects of batch normalization on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 verdicts. A theorem outside V1's specified systems and datasets does not establish support, and untested benchmarks or recipes do not establish limits_scope. The MNIST kernel-value experiment does not measure any version's training outcome.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, Adam, random labels, and comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. The paper's result is theoretical, for fully connected ReLU networks, SGD, logistic loss, and adversarially corrupted labels under stated assumptions.

rows.subject: DNN defined by Eq. (1)
rows.stage_stated: random Gaussian initialization; trained by SGD
rows.operation_detail: Train the fully connected ReLU DNN with logistic loss on data satisfying Assumptions 1 and 7; Theorem 4 bounds the resulting empirical loss.

conditions.value: training data satisfy Assumption 1 and Assumption 7

rows.uncertainty: with high probability; no numeric probability stated
rows.note: The theorem guarantees arbitrarily small empirical loss under its conditions. It does not report a benchmark classification-error measurement.
rows.check: Theorem 4 establishes arbitrarily small empirical logistic loss under its assumptions, but for fully connected networks rather than V1's convolutional networks on CIFAR. The bound implies training classification error at most δ/log(2) in its own setting; the problem is the system and setting mismatch, not merely the use of logistic loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The result is for a specified fully connected binary-classification setting; it does not test the CIFAR benchmarks, convolutional models, Adam, or the other recipe variations in V1 (R1).
